[F4] [[thm-qftx-proper-fixed-locus-noncompact-localization]]: for a smooth separated finite-type torus variety with finite invariant affine cover and proper fixed locus, the localized Borel–Moore pushforward of an equivariant insertion capped with the fundamental class is its fixed-locus Euler-denominator sum. This mathematical pushforward is not a continuum field-space integral.
associated_steps: 3.1 Let $X_k$ be the stable $U(2)$ ADHM quotient in [F2], of complex dimension $4k$. Extend its torus by a flavor factor $\mathbb C^\times_f$ acting trivially on $X_k$, and let $L_{-\widetilde m}$ be its character line with additive first Chern class $-\widetilde m$. The global insertion is $\alpha_{\widetilde m}=e_{T\times\mathbb C^\times_f}(TX_k\otimes L_{-\widetilde m})$, capped with the complex-oriented fundamental class $[X_k]$. The finite invariant affine atlas remains invariant under this trivial base action; the fixed locus remains finite reduced, hence proper. Every hypothesis of [F4] therefore holds. A point with tangent weights $w_j$ contributes $\prod_j(w_j-\widetilde m)/\prod_jw_j$ to $p_*^{\mathrm{loc}}(\alpha_{\widetilde m}\cap[X_k])$. For $k=1$ these are the four weights at each of the two points in steps 1.1–2.1, giving exactly $C_1$. For $k=0$, $X_0$ is a point, both Euler products are empty and the coefficient is $1$. Thus the mathematical noncompact localized-pushforward coefficient is proved. Identifying this insertion with the physical hypermultiplet sector is the sourced pole prescription [A3], not a consequence of equivariant cohomology. [given, F2, F4, A3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

blocks: [[thm-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-asd-correspondence]]

[A1] The exact rank-two theorem supplies the ordinary framed ASD connection of a regular rank-two datum by its raw forward monad/projection construction, extends it smoothly over infinity, and proves $q_2=-k$. Its exact GAGA, coupled-vanishing and intrinsic normal-form hypotheses are retained in the rank-one raw emptiness deduction. [[thm-qftx-zero-fi-regular-adhm-asd-correspondence]]
associated_steps: 1.1 Stabilize a rank-one raw datum by $W'=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C$, $I'=(I,0)$ and $J'=(J,0)^t$, retaining $V,B_1,B_2$. Then $I'J'=IJ$, $I'I'^\dagger=II^\dagger$ and $J'^\dagger J'=J^\dagger J$. The word span is unchanged and $\ker J'=\ker J$, so both moments and regularity are unchanged. On the finite stereographic chart the raw kernel matrix annihilates the added framing line, and its orthogonal projection is $P_1\oplus1$. Thus [A1] produces a smooth rank-two ASD connection whose restriction to that chart is a line connection plus the flat added line and whose charge is $q_2=-k$. By [F2] its determinant curvature vanishes. On that chart this curvature is exactly the first line's curvature, so the whole rank-two curvature is zero there. Smoothness makes it zero also at infinity, hence $q_2=0$ and $k=0$. Thus no regular rank-one zero-FI datum exists for $k>0$, conditional on the exact retained rank-two input. By [F6], a regular complex rank-one orbit would have such a zero-real-moment representative, so the same emptiness conclusion applies to the complex regular quotient. [A1, F1, F2, F6, algebra]

4.1 A regular raw first-order family with $k>0$ would reduce to a prohibited datum from step 1.1, so none exists; the connection family for $k>0$ has no allowable special fiber by step 1.2. At $k=0$ the rank-zero internal $D$-module and all raw maps are uniquely zero, with trivial internal gauge group. Its forward monad is the constant framed line and its forward connection is $d$, also over $D$. Step 3.1 supplies a unique framed gauge from every first-order connection object to this one. Thus this explicit construction is an equivalence of the two first-order groupoids. Reduction and involution-preserving scalar maps commute with it, because the zero datum and the constant line pull back to themselves and the framed trivializing isomorphism is unique. The same argument after complexifying the real tangent spaces gives zero complexified tangent spaces; it does not assert a correspondence for arbitrary complex connections without the Hermitian real condition. [A1, F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Stabilization intertwines $T$ with the rank-two compact action having framing weights $(h,1)$. In the zero-charge classification, inverse rotations and framing changes send a flat framed object to a flat framed object; the unique framed parallel trivialization identifies it with the same point. Its uniqueness also makes the first-order identifications equivariant. They hold for every first-order Hermitian family defined above, hence also for the subset satisfying the exact locally-free/cohomology-base-change hypotheses retained in [A1]; no extra family statement is obtained from an orbit-set bijection. Positive-FI rank-one stable data and their non-locally-free sheaves and formal fixed-point series were not used in any step. [A1, F1, step 1.2, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

blocks: [F2] The finite-holonomy lemma states that $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is open and supplies finite based loops witnessing each irreducible connection. Its complete authored proof and exact batch-56 inputs were inspected; the configuration and stabilizer suppliers now have current ready Step 1 records ([[lem-qftx-irreducible-finite-holonomy-witness]]).
associated_steps: 1.1 If $K=\varnothing$ or $f(K)\subseteq\mathcal A_\infty^*$, the constant homotopy suffices. Otherwise realize the given finite simplicial complex by its barycentric coordinates as a compact subset of $\mathbb R^q$, taking $q\ge1$. Let $U=f^{-1}(\mathcal A_\infty^*)$, an open neighborhood of $L$ by [F2]. Choose nested relatively open neighborhoods $U_0,U_1,U_2$ of $L$ in $K$ with $\overline U_0\subset U_1$, $\overline U_1\subset U_2$, and $\overline U_2\subset U$; if $L=\varnothing$ take them empty. The compact family $f(\overline U_2)$ is uniformly stable under a sufficiently small $C^1$ perturbation: each member has the finite-loop positive margin in [F2], and a finite subcover gives one positive tolerance. Include this $C^1$ norm among the finitely many seminorms in which all forthcoming approximations are to be small. [A1, F1, F2, given, cases, construct]

3.1 Choose a smooth ambient cutoff $0\le\theta\le1$ which is zero on a neighborhood of $\overline U_0$ and one on a neighborhood of the disjoint compact set $K\setminus U_1$. Such a cutoff follows from finitely many ambient bumps separating the two compact sets. Define on $K$ the continuous family $h(s)=f(s)+\theta(s)(g(s)-f(s))$. The straight interpolation from $f$ to $h$ is fixed near $L$ and is $\delta$-small in every selected seminorm. By the uniform $C^1$ margin in step 1.1, choosing $\delta$ small ensures it is irreducible on $\overline U_2$. Its closed reducible-parameter set $R=\{s\in K:h(s)\notin\mathcal A_\infty^*\}$ is compact and contained in $K\setminus U_2$, hence in the ambient open region where $\theta=1$ and $h=g$ on $K$. If $R$ is empty the first interpolation already proves the result. Otherwise choose an ambient open $W$ with compact closure in $V\cap\{\theta=1\}$, containing $R$ and avoiding a neighborhood of $L$, and a smooth cutoff $0\le\chi\le1$ with compact support $T\subset W$, positive on $R$. All subsequent holonomy calculations use the ambient family $g$ on $W$; on the actual parameter subset $K\cap W$ this is exactly $h$. [F1, F2, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct]

10.1 Define on all of $K$ the final family $h_v(s)=h(s)+\chi(s)\sum_{j,a}v_{j,a}b_{j,a}(s)$, with the added term zero off $W$. The compact support $T$ and its spatial smoothness make this term continuous in every section seminorm, and its value uniformly small in any specified finite list by taking $v$ sufficiently small. If $\chi(s)>0$, then $s\in W$ and $h(s)=g(s)$, so $h_v(s)$ has the holonomy tuple $\Phi(s,v)$, which has no common invariant proper subspace by step 9.1. Therefore $h_v(s)$ is irreducible. If $\chi(s)=0$, then $s\notin R$ since $\chi$ is positive on $R$, so $h_v(s)=h(s)$ was already irreducible. The straight perturbation homotopy from $h$ to $h_v$ is fixed on an open neighborhood of $L$. Concatenate it with the interpolation in step 3.1. Choose $\delta$ and then $v$ within half of each requested seminorm tolerance; the triangle inequality gives the asserted bounds relative to the original $f$ for the entire concatenated homotopy. All formulas are global on $K$, so faces and cofaces agree automatically. [F1, F2, F9, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 9.1, construct, algebra] ∎

blocks: [A1] [[post-qftx-nonabelian-yang-mills-model]]: $M$ has the fixed Minkowski metric and orientation in the Statement.

[A2] [[post-qftx-nonabelian-yang-mills-model]]: the global group is $SU(2)$, $P$ is the selected right principal bundle, there are no matter fields, and $\kappa$ is the normalized positive $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant form.

associated_steps:
1.1 Put $H^\Phi=d\Phi(H)$ and let $\omega^\Phi$ be its connection form. Equivariance of $\Phi$ gives $d\Phi_p(Z_P(p))=Z_P(\Phi(p))$ for every $Z\in\mathfrak{su}(2)$. Since $d\Phi$ transports both the vertical and horizontal summands, their projections commute with $d\Phi$; the defining formula $\omega=\zeta^{-1}v$ therefore gives
$\omega^\Phi_{\Phi(p)}(d\Phi_pX)=\omega_p(X)$ for every $X\in T_pP$. [A2, F2, F4, construct]

4.1 The Hodge operator acts on the spacetime-form factors and commutes pointwise with the adjoint action. By [F1],
$\kappa(F_i^\Phi\wedge *_\eta F_i^\Phi)
=\kappa(\operatorname{Ad}_{v_i^{-1}}F_i\wedge *_\eta\operatorname{Ad}_{v_i^{-1}}F_i)
=\kappa(F_i\wedge *_\eta F_i)$
on every trivializing set. These equal local scalar four-forms define the same global action density by the adjoint-bundle pairing, so their integrals over every region where the action is defined agree. No boundary term is introduced because the density is unchanged pointwise. [A1, A3, F1, F6, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

blocks: [A1] [[post-qftx-nonabelian-yang-mills-model]]: $M$ has the fixed Minkowski metric and orientation in the Statement.
[A3] [[post-qftx-nonabelian-yang-mills-model]]: the adopted action density is $-\kappa(F\wedge *_\eta F)/(2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2)$.
[A4] [[post-qftx-nonabelian-yang-mills-model]]: variations are smooth and compactly supported; no boundary values are imposed at infinity, and finite-region variations vanish near the boundary.
associated_steps:
2.1 The difference of the two action densities vanishes outside the compact support of $a$ and its derivatives. Apply the parameter-differentiation clause of [F5] to its smooth coordinate coefficients. Symmetry of $\kappa$ and the even degree of $F_i$ then give
$\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_0\Delta(S/\hbar)_i(\varepsilon;a)
=-\frac{1}{g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int
\kappa(D_{A_i}a\wedge *_\eta F_i)$. [A1, A3, A4, F1, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Write the compactly supported scalar three-form as
$\kappa(a\wedge *_\eta F_i)=\sum_{\mu=0}^3h_\mu\widehat{dx^\mu}$ with
$h_\mu\in C_c^1(U_i)$. Its exterior derivative is
$\sum_\mu(\partial_\mu h_\mu)d^4x$. Apply the integration-by-parts clause
of [F5] with the constant function $1$ to each coefficient $h_\mu$; each
integral is zero, so $\int d\kappa(a\wedge *_\eta F_i)=0$. Substitution in
step 2.1 yields
$\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_0\Delta(S/\hbar)_i(\varepsilon;a)
=-\frac{1}{g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int
\kappa(a\wedge D_{A_i} *_\eta F_i)$. [A1, A4, F5, step 2.1, step 1.2]
4.1 If $D_{A_i} *_\eta F_i=0$, step 3.1 shows that the first variation vanishes for every compactly supported $a$ in every chart. Thus the connection is stationary. [A3, step 3.1, algebra]

4.2 Conversely, assume stationarity. In a local coordinate chart and the orthonormal basis from [F1], write
$J_i=D_{A_i} *_\eta F_i
=\sum_{\mu=0}^3\sum_{b=1}^3J_{\mu b}T_b\,\widehat{dx^\mu}$,
where $\widehat{dx^\mu}$ is the oriented coordinate three-form satisfying
$dx^\mu\wedge\widehat{dx^\mu}=d^4x$. For fixed $\mu,b$, choose
$a=\psi T_b dx^\mu$ with arbitrary smooth compactly supported real $\psi$.
Stationarity and step 3.1 give $\int\psi J_{\mu b}\,d^4x=0$ for every such
$\psi$. The fundamental-lemma clause of [F5] implies $J_{\mu b}=0$
throughout the chart. All coefficients vanish, so the local equation holds.
[A4, F1, F5, step 3.1, algebra]

$*_\eta(dx^1\wedge dx^2)=dx^0\wedge dx^3$. Therefore
$\kappa(F\wedge *_\eta F)
=a^4\kappa(T_3,T_3)\,
dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^0\wedge dx^3
=a^4\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$;
the last reordering is even. Multiplying by the adopted coefficient gives

blocks: [F1] [[post-qftx-nonabelian-yang-mills-model]]: each model instance may select the trivial bundle $P=\mathbb R^{1,3}\times SU(2)$, and the local curvature convention is $F=dA+\frac12[A\wedge A]$.

associated_steps:
1.1 The section-transition law in [F3], applied to $s^u=su$ and $A=0$, gives
$A^u=u^{-1}du$. Since $u=\exp(T_3\sin(x^0/\ell))$ and $T_3$ commutes with itself, differentiation yields
$u^{-1}du=T_3\ell^{-1}\cos(x^0/\ell)\,dx^0$. If the phase were constant,
the same formula would give the zero potential; the chosen sine has
nonzero derivative, so $A^u$ is nonzero. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 The coefficient of $A^u$ depends only on $x^0$ and its one-form factor is $dx^0$, so $dA^u=0$. Every value of $A^u$ is proportional to $T_3$, hence $[A^u\wedge A^u]=0$ by [F2]. The Cartan formula in [F3] gives $F^u=0$, and therefore $\kappa(F^u\wedge *_\eta F^u)=0$. The asserted zero density is exact for this classical field. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

blocks: [F1] [[post-qftx-nonabelian-yang-mills-model]]: the metric is $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the orientation is $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and the action density uses the positive invariant form $\kappa$.
[A1] [[post-qftx-nonabelian-yang-mills-model]]: the local action density is $-\kappa(F\wedge *_\eta F)/(2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2)$.
associated_steps:
1.1 Write $q=x^0-x^3$. Since the coefficient depends only on $q$,
$dA=T_3(b/\ell)\cos(q/\ell)(dx^0-dx^3)\wedge dx^1$. The bracket term
vanishes because $[T_3,T_3]=0$, so this is $F$; it is not identically zero
because $b\ne0$; if $b=0$, both the potential and curvature vanish.
[F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 The Lorentzian Hodge operator for the stated orientation gives
$*_\eta((dx^0-dx^3)\wedge dx^1)=-(dx^0-dx^3)\wedge dx^2$. Hence
$*_\eta F=-T_3(b/\ell)\cos(q/\ell)(dx^0-dx^3)\wedge dx^2$. Its exterior
derivative vanishes because differentiating its coefficient contributes a

By [F9] that complex has zero cohomology for $1\le q\le N$, and its terms are zero above degree $N$. Hence $H^q(D,\mathcal O_D)=0$ for every $q>0$. [A1, F7, F8, F9, given]

blocks: [[def-qftx-wilsonian-n1-action-data|local N=1 Wilsonian action data]]

[F1] [[def-qftx-wilsonian-n1-action-data]]: the bare density contains the canonical matter kinetic term $\sum_i\Phi_i^\dagger e^{-V_i}\Phi_i$, an additional real gauge-invariant $G$, and the chiral term $\tau\operatorname{Tr}(W^\alpha W_\alpha)/(8\pi i)+F(\Phi,W)$; the selected cutoff prescription explicitly assumes a local background-spurion extension, a local derivative expansion and one-particle-irreducible vertex coefficients, without proving generic partial integration has these properties.

[F5] [[def-qftx-wilsonian-n1-action-data]]: in a two-derivative scalar sector, $K(\phi,\bar\phi)$ is a real Kähler potential and $g_{i\bar j}=\partial^2K/(\partial\phi_i\partial\bar\phi_j)$ is its Hermitian metric; both are real D-term data, not holomorphic F-term data.
associated_steps: 1.1 By [F1], [F4], and [A2], the local Wilsonian density at every perturbative order has the same superspace and gauge-invariant decomposition into the fixed canonical matter kinetic term, an additional real D-term, a chiral F-term, and the separately displayed holomorphic gauge-kinetic term. The BRST differential used to state gauge invariance is well-defined and nilpotent by [F2] and [F3]; this is a premise about the local gauge algebra, not a proof of quantum anomaly cancellation. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, A2]

2.1 Use the local background extension in [F1] and [A3], before specializing the external superfields to constant scalars. A derivative-free local chiral coefficient cannot depend on an unconstrained real background $P$: applying $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}$ to such a coefficient gives its derivative with respect to $P$ times the independent odd background jet $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}P$, so chirality forces that derivative to vanish. Terms involving background superderivatives instead have a chiral projection and lie in the D-sector of the stated derivative expansion. The usual factorization $P=Z^\dagger Z e^{V_P}$ does not circumvent this argument. On a patch with positive scalar body, choose any invertible chiral external $Z$ and define the real $V_P=\log P-\log Z-\log Z^\dagger$ by its ordinary body logarithm and finite nilpotent expansion. This merely parametrizes the same external $P$; $Z$ and $V_P$ are not independent physical couplings. In particular $Z\mapsto e^{i\alpha}Z$ leaves $P$ and every regulated coefficient written in the original backgrounds unchanged, with all integrated fields held fixed. A holomorphic chiral coefficient independent of the unconstrained real $V_P$ cannot acquire nonconstant dependence on the dummy $Z$: for a holomorphic function $f$, invariance under every phase implies $Z\partial_Zf=0$. A field-independent quadratic gauge chiral term may change by the topological-angle total derivative; keep this separately in the displayed $\tau_\lambda$ gauge parameter. This is a statement about the local action modulo its stated boundary terms, not an assertion about a Jacobian from rescaling charged fields. Thus the original real D coefficients do not enter the derivative-free $F_\lambda$. Analyticity in [A3] extends the identity on the positive-body patch to the formal coefficient domain. [F1, A1, A2, A3, algebra, step 1.1]

4.1 Consider a connected graph contributing to this chiral density, with $E_V$ external left-handed gaugino lines and $I_V$ internal vector lines. Let $A_m$ count pure-gauge vertices from the quadratic $W^\alpha W_\alpha$ term with $m\geq3$ vector lines; let $B_{mr}$ count vertices from an F-term containing $r$ field strengths and $m\geq r$ vector lines; and let $C_m$ count vertices from the fixed canonical matter kinetic term with two chiral lines and $m\geq1$ vector lines. Counting vector-line ends gives $2I_V+E_V=\sum_{m\geq3}mA_m+\sum_r\sum_{m\geq r}mB_{mr}+\sum_{m\geq1}mC_m$. The R-charge condition gives $\sum_r\sum_{m\geq r}(2-r)B_{mr}=2-E_V$. Each vector propagator contributes one factor $\tau^{-1}$ and each pure-gauge vertex one factor $\tau$, so $N_\tau=\sum_{m\geq3}A_m-I_V$; eliminating $E_V$ and $I_V$ yields $N_\tau=1-\tfrac12[\sum_{m\geq3}(m-2)A_m+\sum_r\sum_{m\geq r}(2-r+m)B_{mr}+\sum_{m\geq1}mC_m]$. [F1, A2, A3, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Every coefficient inside the square brackets is a positive integer. A graph contributing to the $\tau$-independent part $H_\lambda$ must have $N_\tau=0$, so the bracket equals two. The positive-integer solutions are two cubic or one quartic pure-gauge vertices, one $B_{mr}$ vertex with $m=r$, two $C_1$ vertices, one $C_2$ vertex, or the mixed case with one cubic gauge vertex and one $C_1$ vertex. For the $B_{mr}$ case, [step 4.1]'s R-charge equation gives $E_V=r=m$; the vector-end equation then gives $I_V=0$. It is the original single tree insertion. In the $A_3=2$ pure-gauge case the R-charge equation gives $E_V=2$ and the vector-end equation is $2I_V+2=6$, so $I_V=2$ and $L=2-2+1=1$. In the $A_4=1$ case it is $2I_V+2=4$, so $I_V=1$ and $L=1-1+1=1$. Both are one-particle-irreducible contributions to the gauge-kinetic term. For either matter-only case, the R-charge equation gives $E_V=2$ and the vector-end equation gives $2I_V+2=2$, so $I_V=0$. Each $C_m$ vertex contains one chiral and one antichiral matter line. A contribution to a holomorphic F-term cannot have an external antichiral line; with no other vertex type present, the two $C_1$ vertices therefore contract their two antichiral ends with their two chiral ends, giving $I_\Phi=2$, while the one $C_2$ vertex contracts its own chiral/antichiral pair, giving $I_\Phi=1$. Thus in each case the total internal-line count equals the vertex count and $L=1$; no matter line is external, so these graphs correct only the field-independent gauge-kinetic term. In the mixed case the end equation is $2I_V+2=3+1=4$, so $I_V=1$; the single $C_1$ vertex contracts its chiral/antichiral pair, giving $I_\Phi=1$. Hence $I=2$, $N_{\rm vert}=2$, and $L=1$. Its sole vector line is a bridge separating the gauge vertex from the matter vertex, so it is one-particle-reducible and excluded by the vertex convention in [F1]. Therefore the only tree contribution is the original $F$, every other allowed contribution is a one-loop gauge-kinetic correction that shifts the separately displayed $\tau_\lambda$, and no higher-loop correction is possible. A graph contributing to an additional $c_\lambda\tau W^2$ term would require $N_\tau=1$, hence a zero bracket and no vertices, which cannot form a graph with external fields; therefore $c_\lambda=0$. [F1, A2, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 For an unbroken U(1) factor, the prepotential shifts by $V_1\mapsto V_1-\Lambda_1-\bar\Lambda_1$. A constant coefficient $\xi$ multiplying $\int d^4x\,[V_1]_D$ is gauge invariant because the Berezin integral of the chiral and anti-chiral shifts vanishes under the boundary condition in [F1]. For a field-independent coefficient promoted to a real spurion $S$, the physical variation contains $-[P_{\mathrm{phys}}(S)\Lambda_1]_F$ and its Hermitian conjugate, where $P_{\mathrm{phys}}=-\tfrac12\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot2}}\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot1}}|_{\bar\theta=0}=+\tfrac14\bar D^{\dot\alpha}\bar D_{\dot\alpha}$ at fixed chiral coordinates is the normalized D-to-F projector in [F1]; invariance for arbitrary chiral $\Lambda_1$ forces the spurion components relevant to this operator to be constant. A separately specified field-dependent linear-multiplet coupling is not this FI coefficient and remains part of $G_\lambda$ by [A4]. Therefore a correction to the constant FI coefficient must be independent of the coupling spurions in [A3]. The only such candidate is the matter tadpole from the canonical kinetic vertex. Since all masses and interactions are spurions, this coupling-independent regulated integral is the same for each chiral component; the representation enters only through its charge. Writing its common value as $C_\lambda$, the correction is $\delta\xi^{(1)}=C_\lambda\sum_i q_i$. This is a one-loop graph, so the correction vanishes when the charge sum is zero and there are no higher-loop FI graphs. [F1, A2, A3, A4, step 5.1]

7.1 The argument constrains the chiral integrand and the FI tadpole only; it places no equality requirement on the arbitrary real function $G_\lambda$ in [F1] or on the real Kähler data in [F5]. Since the high-mode split retains momenta below $\lambda$ and [A1] excludes nonperturbative sectors, no conclusion follows for an arbitrary one-particle-irreducible functional, instanton corrections, coefficients after field rescaling, or a continuum limit. These are exactly the qualifications in the statement. [F1, F5, A1, step 1.1, step 5.1, step 6.1] ∎

associated_steps: 1.1 For a block $b$ with $\lambda_b>0$, let $K_b=(Q+S)|_{\mathcal H_b}$. The actual adjoint/domain and reducing-block hypotheses make this an everywhere-defined odd self-adjoint finite-dimensional operator. Since $Q^2=S^2=0$ and $\delta=2(SQ+QS)$, $K_b^2=\lambda_b I/2$. Thus $B_b=\sqrt{2/\lambda_b}K_b$ is a unitary odd involution exchanging the two block parity spaces. This uses this page's supercharge normalization, not the differently normalized right-handed charge on the index page. [given, F1, A1, algebra]

2.1 The restriction $U_b$ commutes with $K_b$. Its even and odd restrictions are therefore unitarily conjugate by $B_b$ and have equal finite traces. The signed contribution from this block, including its common heat factor, is zero. The full weighted operator is trace class by [A1], so its basis diagonal is absolutely summable; regrouping by the countable blocks preserves the sum. Only zero-gap blocks contribute, even if infinitely many blocks share a gap. [given, F1, A1, step 1.1, algebra]

blocks: [F1] [[def-qftx-scft-protected-data]]: on a scalar primary, the two adjoint supercharge anticommutators reduce to $2\{S,Q\}=D-\tfrac32R$ and $2\{\bar S,\bar Q\}=D+\tfrac32R$, with $S=Q^\dagger$ and $\bar S=\bar Q^\dagger$.
associated_steps: 1.1 Using $S|\mathcal O\rangle=0$ and the Hilbert-adjoint relation, [F1] gives $(d_{\mathcal O}-\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O})\|\mathcal O\|^2=\langle\mathcal O|2\{S,Q\}|\mathcal O\rangle=2\|Q\mathcal O\|^2\geq0$. Thus $d_{\mathcal O}\geq\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O}$, with equality exactly when $Q|\mathcal O\rangle=0$. [given, F1, A1, algebra]

2.1 The conjugate anticommutator similarly gives $(d_{\mathcal O}+\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O})\|\mathcal O\|^2=\langle\mathcal O|2\{\bar S,\bar Q\}|\mathcal O\rangle=2\|\bar Q\mathcal O\|^2\geq0$. Combining the two inequalities gives $d_{\mathcal O}\geq\max(\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O},-\tfrac32r_{\mathcal O})=\tfrac32|r_{\mathcal O}|$; the active equality condition is the first norm when $r_{\mathcal O}\geq0$ and the conjugate norm when $r_{\mathcal O}\leq0$. [given, F1, A1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

associated_steps: 1.1 The three nonzero elements of $\mathcal C$ are $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, and $(1,1)$. Each generates an order-two subgroup with the origin. The pairing is alternating, so each such subgroup is isotropic. Any subgroup containing two distinct nonzero elements contains two linearly independent columns in $\mathbb Z_2^2$; the determinant $em'-me'$ of two independent columns is nonzero and therefore equals $1$ in $\mathbb Z_2$. Hence such a subgroup is not isotropic. Therefore these are exactly the three maximal isotropic subgroups, and [F2] gives their source-reported gauge-group labels. [given, F1, F2, A1, algebra]

2.1 Modulo $2$, the map $S$ sends $(1,0)$ to $(0,1)$, $(0,1)$ to $(1,0)$, and $(1,1)$ to $(1,1)$. The map $T$ sends $(1,0)$ to $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$ to $(1,1)$, and $(1,1)$ to $(0,1)$. These invertible linear maps therefore send the displayed subgroups exactly as stated. Their coupling transformations and physical interpretation as dualities are the source-reported conjectural inputs [F2], not consequences of the finite arithmetic. [given, F1, F2, A1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

associated_steps: 1.1 From $Q|b\rangle=\sqrt{\lambda/2}|f\rangle$, $Q|f\rangle=0$, and $S=Q^\dagger$, we have $SQ|b\rangle=(\lambda/2)|b\rangle$, $QS|b\rangle=0$, $SQ|f\rangle=0$, and $QS|f\rangle=(\lambda/2)|f\rangle$. associated_steps:
1.1 Differentiating $W_\mu=\sqrt2 A_D M\widetilde M+\mu u(A_D)$ gives
$F_{A_D}=\sqrt2 M\widetilde M+\mu u'(A_D)$,
$F_M=\sqrt2 A_D\widetilde M$, and
$F_{\widetilde M}=\sqrt2 A_DM$. At $A_D=0$, the first equation is

2.1 Set $v=(|\mu c|/\sqrt2)^{1/2}>0$ and

$|\widetilde M|=|\mu c|/(\sqrt2v)=v$, so all F equations and

[F1] [[post-aqft-smeft-model]]: $H$ is a smooth complex doublet of hypercharge $Y=1/2$ (integer charge $y=3$), and its conjugate is $\widetilde H=i\sigma^2H^*$; the adopted field content, unit conventions and direct-product gauge action are fixed there.
associated_steps: 1.1 For $H=(a,b)^T\ne0$, let $\rho=(H^\dagger H)^{1/2}>0$. Direct multiplication gives $\Sigma=(i\sigma^2H^*,H)=\begin{pmatrix}b^*&a\\-a^*&b\end{pmatrix}$, so $\Sigma^\dagger\Sigma=(|a|^2+|b|^2)I=\rho^2I$ and $\det\Sigma=|a|^2+|b|^2=\rho^2$. Therefore $U=\Sigma/\rho$ is unitary with determinant one, hence lies in $SU(2)$, and $h=\sqrt2\rho-v>-v$ lies in $J$. The map $\Phi$ is smooth by scalar and matrix multiplication. Also $H^\dagger H$ is smooth and positive on $\mathbb C^2\setminus\{0\}$, $s\mapsto\sqrt{s}$ is smooth on $(0,\infty)$, and division by $\rho>0$ is smooth, so the displayed inverse is smooth. Conversely, direct multiplication for an $SU(2)$ matrix gives $i\sigma^2U^*=Ui\sigma^2$ and $i\sigma^2e_2=e_1$, so $\Sigma(\Phi(h,U))=(v+h)U/\sqrt2$ and $\rho(\Phi(h,U))=(v+h)/\sqrt2$. These identities show that the two formulas compose to the identity in both directions. Thus $\Phi$ is a smooth diffeomorphism onto precisely the nonzero-doublet patch. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 For $g_L\in SU(2)$, the defining two-dimensional representation obeys $i\sigma^2g_L^*=g_Li\sigma^2$; this follows by writing $g_L=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\-b^*&a^*\end{pmatrix}$ and multiplying. Since $H\mapsto g_Lz^3H$, this identity gives $\widetilde H\mapsto g_Lz^{-3}\widetilde H$. Consequently $\Sigma\mapsto g_L\Sigma\operatorname{diag}(z^{-3},z^3)=g_L\Sigma g_R(z)^{-1}$. Unitarity preserves $\rho$, so $h$ is unchanged and $U=\Sigma/\rho$ has exactly the HEFT transformation law in [F2]. Hence $\Phi$ is equivariant. [given, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

1.3 The doublet derivative is $D_\mu H=\partial_\mu H+igW_\mu H+\tfrac{i}{2}g'B_\mu H$, because $Y(H)=1/2$. Applying the product rule to $H=(v+h)Ue_2/\sqrt2$ and using $T_3e_2=-e_2/2$ in the $D_\mu U$ formula of [F2] yields
$$D_\mu H=\frac1{\sqrt2}\left((\partial_\mu h)Ue_2+(v+h)D_\mu Ue_2\right).$$
The conjugate formula follows by complex conjugation. Repeated covariant derivatives expand into finite sums by the product rule, and field strengths remain the same curvature polynomials under this substitution. Thus every selected local polynomial representative has a finite HEFT expansion. [given, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

[F1] [[post-aqft-smeft-model]]: the spacetime metric is $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the Higgs kinetic term is $-(D_\mu H)^\dagger D^\mu H$, and $v$, $g$, and $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ have the units and meanings stated in the model.

[F5] [[post-aqft-smeft-model]]: if $v$ is interpreted as a vacuum radius, the supplied scalar-potential coefficients are assumed to make $H^\dagger H=v^2/2$ a local minimum; the model does not derive this parameter condition.
associated_steps: 1.3 The renormalizable radial kinetic density is $-\tfrac12\partial_\mu h\partial^\mu h$. Adding the result of step 1.2 gives $-\tfrac12K(h)\partial_\mu h\partial^\mu h$ with $K(h)=1+2C_{H\Box}(v+h)^2/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^2$. Since $C_{H\Box}$ is dimensionless and both $v+h$ and $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ have mass dimension one, $K$ is dimensionless. Under [A3], $K>0$ near zero. [given, F1, F2, A3, step 1.2, algebra]

1.4 With $U=I$, write $r=v+h$ and use $T_a=\sigma_a/2$. The upper component of the covariant derivative is $(D_\mu H)_1=ig r(W_\mu^1-iW_\mu^2)/(2\sqrt2)=ig rW_\mu^+/2$. Since $W^1,W^2$ are real, its norm squared is $g^2r^2W_\mu^-W^{+\mu}/4$. The Higgs kinetic term therefore contains $-g^2r^2W_\mu^+W^{-\mu}/4$. The chosen $Q_{H\Box}$ has no gauge field, so this coefficient is unchanged as a function of $h$; thus $m_W^2(h)=g^2(v+h)^2/4$ and $m_W^2(0)=g^2v^2/4$. [given, A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

1.5 On an interval with $K>0$, $\widehat h'(h)=\sqrt{K(h)}>0$ and $\widehat h(0)=0$. For $h_1<h_2$, $\widehat h(h_2)-\widehat h(h_1)=\int_{h_1}^{h_2}\sqrt{K(s)}\,ds>0$, so $\widehat h$ is strictly increasing and maps a neighborhood of zero onto an interval with a continuous inverse. At every $h_0$ in this interval, the inverse difference quotient tends to $1/\widehat h'(h_0)$; hence its derivative is $1/\sqrt{K(\widehat h^{-1}(y))}$. This derivative is continuous, and induction in that identity makes the inverse smooth because $K$ and the square root are smooth where $K>0$. Also $\widehat h(h)/h\to\sqrt{K(0)}$ as $h\to0$. Hence the difference quotient in the new coordinate is
$$\lim_{h\to0}\frac{m_W^2(h)-m_W^2(0)}{\widehat h(h)-\widehat h(0)}=\frac{(dm_W^2/dh)|_0}{\widehat h'(0)}=\frac{g^2v/2}{\sqrt{K(0)}}.$$
Since $2m_W^2(0)/v=g^2v/2$, the defined coupling is $\kappa_W=1/\sqrt{K(0)}$, which yields the displayed expression. If this reference point is called a vacuum, the supplied potential must satisfy [F5]; otherwise the result is only a local expansion coefficient. It supplies no empirical measurement or numerical bound on discarded orders. [given, F4, F5, A1, A3, A4, step 1.3, step 1.4, algebra] ∎

[F1] [[def-aqft-susy-wilsonian-action]]: light and heavy chiral multiplets are smooth classical N=1 superfields with fixed engineering dimensions; the Wilsonian F-term is distinct from real D-term data, and operator-suppression and threshold scales are separate.
associated_steps: 2.1 With $[\phi]=1$, $[F_{\mathcal X}]=2$, and $[\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}]=1$, the coefficient $A_{\mathrm{soft}}=\kappa F_{\mathcal X}/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ has dimension one and the scalar cubic term has dimension four. For $F_{\mathcal X}\ne0$, the left derivative gives $Q_1(2\theta^1\theta^2F_{\mathcal X})=2\theta^2F_{\mathcal X}\ne0$, so fixing this background breaks rigid supersymmetry. The Ward-identity hypothesis of [F5] then fails, and that theorem supplies no protection claim for the fixed soft coefficient. Full AC is inherited only for the selected operator-equivalence interpretation [A1]; no choice is used in this component calculation. No estimate of the soft coefficient's size follows from its dimension. [F1, F5, A1, A2, A3, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

blocks: [F1] [[pthm-aqft-symmetry-preserving-rg-anomaly-match]]: the matching conclusion assumes the same exact global symmetry is unbroken along the RG comparison.
associated_steps: 2.1 Choose the allowed configuration $\phi_x=ir$ at every site with real $r\neq0$. The derivative of the full source term is $-2a^4j r N^4\neq0$. Therefore the fixed-source action is not invariant under $U(1)$, so this model cannot be the endpoint of an exact $U(1)$-preserving flow as required by [F1]. blocks: Physical BPS charge and second-helicity index data: [[def-qftx-physical-bps-charge-data]].

[F1] [[def-qftx-physical-bps-charge-data]]: on a regular patch the formal label lattice is $\mathbb Z^2$, $z_u(n_e,n_m)=\sqrt2(n_ea+n_ma_D)$, the chosen DSZ form is integral and antisymmetric, and $\Omega_u(\gamma)$ is the second-helicity supertrace on the supplied one-particle BPS sector.
associated_steps: 1.1 For a supported charge $\gamma$, put $n_\delta=\Omega_u(\gamma)\langle\delta,\gamma\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}\in\mathbb Z$. Since $\ell(\gamma)>0$, the binomial expansion of $1-\varepsilon(\gamma)y^\gamma$ to any integer power is defined degreewise in the pointed completion: terms of order $k$ have degree increased by $k\ell(\gamma)$. Bilinearity gives $n_{\delta+\delta'}=n_\delta+n_{\delta'}$, so the formula for $\mathcal K_{\gamma,u}$ is multiplicative on monomials and hence on series by continuity. It fixes $y^\gamma$ because the pairing is alternating, and replacing $n_\delta$ by $-n_\delta$ gives its inverse. Finite sublevels and $\ell(\gamma)>0$ ensure each bounded-degree output uses only finitely many input terms and binomial terms. Local finiteness of the support then makes the phase-ordered composition $\mathcal S_u$ continuous and well-defined. [F1, A3, given, algebra]

3.1 Since $\Theta$ is a continuous group homomorphism on units, applying it to step 2.1 preserves equality. The Hall generator is the decreasing-phase product of the factors $J(S_{Z_u}(\phi))$; multiplicativity of $\Phi$ and $\Theta$ and the per-phase identity in [A2] therefore identify each image with the corresponding physical phase factor, in the same order. Degreewise continuity and local finiteness in [A3] pass this equality from finite truncations to the full products. [F1] supplies the second-helicity index convention, and [A1] records its choice-strength premise. Thus $\mathcal S_{u_-}=\mathcal S_{u_+}$. [A1, A2, A3, F1, F2, step 2.1] ∎

blocks: Physical charge labels, central charge, and DSZ pairing: [[def-qftx-physical-bps-charge-data]].

[F3] [[def-qftx-physical-bps-charge-data]]: $\gamma_m=(0,1)$, $\gamma_d=(1,-1)$, the scalar central charges are $z_m=\sqrt2a_D$ and $z_d=\sqrt2(a-a_D)$, and $\langle\gamma_m,\gamma_d\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=2$.
associated_steps: 4.1 The charge map preserves the skew form on the basis pair: the two-arrow orientation gives $\langle\mathbf e_m,\mathbf e_d\rangle_Q=2$, equal to $\langle\gamma_m,\gamma_d\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}$ by [F3]. Applying [F5] to the two phase assignments proves equality of the full completed Hall generators. If the bridge in [F6] is supplied with these exact phases and pairings, the physical KS products agree by the conditional theorem. The coefficient $(q+1)/(q-1)$ remains the finite-field groupoid weight computed in step 3.1; no step identifies it with the physical index $\Omega_u(\gamma_m+\gamma_d)$. [A1, F3, F5, F6, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

blocks: [F1] The nonlinear magnetostatic datum defines $H=\sqrt2M\widetilde M+\mu u'(a)$, $d=|M|^2-|\widetilde M|^2$, $s=|M|^2+|\widetilde M|^2$, $V_b=b^{-1}|H|^2+d^2/(2b)+2|a|^2s$, the small-disk and positive-metric bounds, and the exact broad admissible class with uniform vacuum approach. [[def-qftx-n2-nonlinear-magnetostatic-flux-cylinder]]
associated_steps: 1.1 Put $x=\sqrt2M\widetilde M$ and $U_0=\mu c$, so $s^2=d^2+2|x|^2$ and $\xi=\sqrt2|U_0|$. By the fundamental theorem of calculus along the segment from $0$ to $a$ inside the convex disk, $|\mu(u'(a)-c)|\le K|a|$. If $s\le t_*$, then $|x|\le s/\sqrt2\le m_*/2$, whereas the disk hypothesis gives $|\mu u'(a)|\ge m_*$. Hence $|H|\ge m_*/2$ and $V_b\ge m_*^2/(4b_+)\ge[m_*^2/(4b_+\xi^2)](s-\xi)^2$, since $s\le t_*\le\xi/2$. If $s\ge t_*$, the reverse triangle inequality in $\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb C$ gives $(s-\xi)^2\le d^2+2|x+U_0|^2\le d^2+4|H|^2+4K^2|a|^2$. The three terms are bounded by $2b_+V_b$, $4b_+V_b$, and $2K^2V_b/t_*$, respectively, because $V_b\ge2|a|^2s\ge2t_*|a|^2$. Combining the cases proves the stated uniform potential bound without a Hessian or minimizer assumption. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 Use the unitary real-linear change $q=(M+e^{i\beta}\overline{\widetilde M})/\sqrt2$, $p=(M-e^{i\beta}\overline{\widetilde M})/\sqrt2$; both fields have charge +1 and $s=|q|^2+|p|^2$. Their summed covariant-gradient norms equal the original charged norms. Let $E_0$ be the critical two-charge functional with terms $b_0B^2/2+|Dq|^2+|Dp|^2+(s-\xi)^2/(2b_0)$ and no additional p-mass term. The Maxwell bound $b\ge b_-$, step 1.1 and the definition of $\gamma$ give $E_b\ge\gamma E_0$, after dropping the nonnegative neutral gradient. In particular $E_0$ is finite. Uniform vacuum approach makes q,p bounded near infinity, with $|q|\to\sqrt\xi$ and $p\to0$ in the vacuum phase frame. Stokes on disks and the original angular condition give limiting flux $2\pi n$. [given, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Write $G(R)=\int_{|x|=R}(|Dq|^2+|Dp|^2)\,ds$. Finiteness of the gradient integral implies $\int_{R_0}^{\infty}G(R)\,dR<\infty$. There are radii $R_j\to\infty$ with $R_jG(R_j)\to0$: otherwise $G(R)\ge\epsilon/R$ eventually for some $\epsilon>0$, contradicting that integral. By [F3] and bounded tail amplitudes, the absolute boundary-current integral $\oint(\bar qDq+\bar pDp)$ on these circles is at most $C\sqrt{R_jG(R_j)}\to0$. For $n>0$, expand the disk square identity using $[D_1,D_2]f=-iBf$ for $f=q,p$: $|(D_1+iD_2)f|^2=|Df|^2-B|f|^2+i\{\partial_1(\bar fD_2f)-\partial_2(\bar fD_1f)\}$ and $b_0[B-b_0^{-1}(\xi-s)]^2/2=b_0B^2/2+(s-\xi)^2/(2b_0)+Bs-\xi B$. Add the identities, integrate, and let $R_j\to\infty$. The boundary current vanishes along this subsequence, the flux tends to $2\pi n$ and the remaining squares are nonnegative, so $E_0\ge2\pi\xi n$. Reflection of the second transverse coordinate proves $E_0\ge2\pi\xi|n|$ for negative n. Step 2.1 now proves the claimed positive bound for every full-model profile. No full-circle boundary-current limit was assumed or inferred from finite energy. [given, F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Let $N=|n|$. Choose smooth radial functions f,h with f(r) equal to a positive constant times $r^N$ near zero, h(r) equal to a constant times $r^2$ near zero, and f=h=1 outside one fixed disk; choose the near-zero coefficients as smooth functions of $r^2$ and interpolate on a compact annulus. Set $q=\sqrt\xi f(r)e^{in\theta}$, $p=a=0$, and $A=nh(r)d\theta$, hence $M=q/\sqrt2$, $\widetilde M=e^{i\beta}\bar q/\sqrt2$. The charged fields are smooth at zero because $r^Ne^{in\theta}$ is $z^N$ or $\bar z^N$, and the connection is smooth because $r^2d\theta=x^1dx^2-x^2dx^1$. Curvature and every non-vacuum energy term are supported in a fixed disk; all are smooth there. Outside it the field is exactly in the vacuum orbit, the covariant gradients vanish and the angular flux coefficient is n. Thus this is an admitted finite-energy profile. Its energy is positive by step 3.1 and finite directly; consequently $0<\gamma2\pi\xi|n|\le\tau_n<\infty$. [given, F1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 For any profile, M is nonzero outside a disk by uniform vacuum approach. The circle-valued function $(M/|M|)e^{-in\theta}$ has degree zero on that exterior annulus. It has a smooth real phase lift $\chi$: the closed real one-form $-if^{-1}df$ for this circle-valued function f has zero integral on each circle, so integrating first radially and then angularly from a fixed base point defines a smooth periodic lift with $e^{i\chi}=f$. Multiply $-\chi$ by a radial smooth cutoff equal to zero near the inner boundary and one on a larger exterior annulus, then exponentiate to obtain a globally smooth gauge transformation. The transformed fields have $M=m e^{in\theta}$, m>0, and $A=nd\theta+\alpha$ outside a compact set. This gauge change leaves energy and the original angular condition invariant and fixes the exact exterior M-phase; it does not impose a new decay hypothesis. Write $\widetilde M=e^{i\beta}w e^{-in\theta}$, so m,w tend uniformly to v. [given, F1, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 On this exterior, s is bounded below by $\xi/2$ and m by $v/2$. The potential controls $|a|^2\le V_b/\xi$, $d^2\le2b_+V_b$, $|H|^2\le b_+V_b$ and $(s-\xi)^2\le C_VV_b$. Since $m^2-v^2=(s+d-\xi)/2$, $|m-v|^2\le[(s-\xi)^2+d^2]/(2v^2)$ is integrable. Also $m w-v^2=e^{-i\beta}[H-\mu(u'(a)-c)]/\sqrt2$, so $|w-v|\le(2/v)\{(|H|+K|a|)/\sqrt2+v|m-v|\}$ is square-integrable. Thus a,m-v,w-v are in $L^2$ on the exterior. Finally $DM=e^{in\theta}(dm-im\alpha)$, with dm and alpha real. Its squared norm is $|dm|^2+m^2|\alpha|^2$, so finite charged energy and m>=v/2 give $\alpha,dm\in L^2$. On compact sets all fields and coefficients are smooth and bounded. Hence any two canonical profiles differ in $L^2$ in a,M,$\widetilde M$ and their connection one-forms. These mass-tail conclusions use uniform approach to the vacuum as well as the finite potential/kinetic energy; finite energy alone was not asserted to force pointwise vacuum approach. [given, F1, step 1.1, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Let two canonical profiles be given and choose one radius beyond both cleanup disks. A smooth cutoff $\eta(t)$, t in [0,ell], constant zero near 0 and one near ell, defines an explicit collar by linearly blending a,M,$\widetilde M$,A_1,A_2 and setting $A_3=0$. The neutral disk is convex, so the blend stays in it. Longitudinal scalar derivatives and $F_{3i}$ are $\eta'$ times the corresponding $L^2$ differences from step 6.1, hence have finite energy. For either charged field f, its transverse covariant derivative along the blend equals the blend of the two original covariant derivatives plus a bounded coefficient times $(A^{(1)}-A^{(0)})(f^{(1)}-f^{(0)})$. The connection difference is $L^2$ and the field difference is bounded globally, so this term is $L^2$; neutral gradients and transverse curvatures also blend linearly. Near infinity the field deviations from the common canonical vacuum frame are $L^2$ and uniformly small. Smoothness of u,b and vanishing of the potential and its first derivatives on that vacuum orbit give the uniform local estimate $V_b\le C(|a|^2+|m-v|^2+|w-v|^2)$ along the blend, by a Taylor formula on one compact transverse slice of the phase orbit. This makes the collar potential integrable; compact interiors have finite energy by smoothness. The exterior M-phase remains exactly $e^{in\theta}$ because its blended amplitude is positive, and $A_\theta-n$ is a convex blend of two functions tending uniformly to zero. Thus winding, angular condition and limiting flux are preserved on every collar slice; uniform covariant-gradient decay is preserved by the same product formula, using $\alpha\to0$ from $DM\to0$ and m>=v/2. This constructs an actual finite-energy collar, with cost independent of any later cylinder length L. [given, F1, step 5.1, step 6.1, construct, algebra]

8.1 The three-dimensional energy is the transverse planar energy on each slice plus nonnegative longitudinal Maxwell and scalar terms. By [F4] and the definition of $\tau_n$, every competitor has $E_{b,3}\ge\tau_nL$. For each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, the definition of the finite infimum provides one planar profile with energy below $\tau_n+\varepsilon$; gauge-clean it by step 5.1. Step 7.1 constructs collars from each fixed end trace to this profile, with one chosen width ell and finite total energy $C_\varepsilon$, independent of L. Concatenate the collars with its translation-invariant extension over length L-2ell. This is a smooth admissible competitor because each collar is constant near the inner face, and it has energy at most $(\tau_n+\varepsilon)(L-2\ell)+C_\varepsilon$. Taking the infimum proves the two-sided bounds. Dividing by L, taking limsup as L tends to infinity and then allowing each $\varepsilon>0$ to tend to zero gives limsup<=tau_n, while the lower bound gives liminf>=tau_n. Hence the limit is tau_n>0. No minimizer or uniform bound on $C_\varepsilon$ as epsilon tends to zero is used, so no generic $O(1)$ remainder follows. [A1, F1, F4, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 7.1, algebra]

9.1 In this specified magnetostatic model all time derivatives and $A_0$ vanish, so the electric field is zero and the charged time-current density vanishes. With constant or absent theta, the Gauss constraint is therefore zero on every constructed trial field, including collars, even when b varies spatially. The slice lower bound remains true on any further constraint subset. In the adopted charge dictionary, the fixed dual magnetic flux is original electric flux, so its positive asymptotic energy per separation proves the stated classical local confinement. It supplies neither the different Gauss law with field-dependent theta nor a statement about arbitrary quantum line operators or microscopic string-breaking processes. [given, F1, step 8.1, algebra] ∎

blocks: [[post-aqft-heft-model|Nonlinear Goldstone field, scalar singlet and smooth HEFT functions]]
[[post-aqft-heft-model|Adopted Minkowski spacetime and mostly-plus metric convention]]
[[def-aqft-heavy-chiral-u1-threshold-data|Selected U(1)_V-singlet model, charge, mass, regulator, and threshold conventions]]

[F1] [[def-aqft-heavy-chiral-u1-threshold-data]]: $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$, $\delta_\alpha\theta=-\alpha$, $G=dB$ is invariant, and $M_H=|y|v>0$; the model adopts the mass-independent anomalous Jacobian as its threshold interpretation.
associated_steps: 1.1 From [F1], $G'=d(B+d\alpha)=G+d^2\alpha=G$, while $\delta_\alpha\theta=-\alpha$. Thus $G\wedge G$ is invariant under the specified small background transformations. [given, F1, algebra]

1.2 In Bilal's Hermitian convention [A1], $\mathscr A=-B$ and $\epsilon=-\alpha$. The linear evaluation $E^4_{0,\alpha}$ of [F3], with component rule $sB_\mu=\partial_\mu\eta$, gives the same infinitesimal four-form variation as [F1]; in Bilal's anti-Hermitian variables this is $-i\mathscr A=iB$ and $-i\epsilon=i\alpha$, matching the product-group charge-one connection. For the positive-chirality $SU(3)$ singlet of $U(1)_V$ charge one in [F3], $\operatorname{tr}_R(1)=1$ and $d(\mathscr A\wedge d\mathscr A)=d(B\wedge G)=G\wedge G$; the Abelian cubic term vanishes. Therefore $\delta_\alpha\Gamma_H=+\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\alpha G\wedge G=\mathcal A_H(\alpha,B)$. The neutral opposite-chirality partner contributes zero $U(1)_V$ cubic charge. [given, F1, F3, A1, algebra]

2.1 Vary the displayed local functional: $\delta_\alpha\Gamma_{\mathrm{WZ}}=-\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M((\delta_\alpha\theta)G\wedge G+\theta\,\delta_\alpha(G\wedge G))=+\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\alpha G\wedge G=\mathcal A_H(\alpha,B)$ by step 1.1 and step 1.2. [F1, A1, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

blocks: [[pthm-aqft-heavy-chiral-threshold-wess-zumino-match|Conditional local threshold-matching theorem and anomaly normalization]]
[F1] [[pthm-aqft-heavy-chiral-threshold-wess-zumino-match]]: the heavy-sector consistent variation and Wess–Zumino variation both equal $+\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\alpha G\wedge G$.
associated_steps: 3.1 Integrating against $\alpha$ and using [A1] gives $\int_M\alpha G\wedge G=2\lambda^2\int_M\alpha\,d^4x=2$. Therefore both variations in [F1] equal $+2/(24\pi^2)=+1/(12\pi^2)$. [F1, A1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

blocks: [F6] A compact perturbation of a Fredholm operator is Fredholm with the same index. [[thm-fredholm-index-is-stable-under-compact-perturbations]]
associated_steps: 2.1 Apply [F3] with $r=k-1\ge0$ to $\Delta_{A_0}:H^{k+1}\to H^{k-1}$. Its kernel is finite dimensional, and the Hodge theorem gives the topological direct decomposition $H^{k-1}=\ker\Delta_{A_0}\oplus\Delta_{A_0}(H^{k+1})$. Thus its range is closed with codimension equal to the kernel dimension, so $\Delta_{A_0}$ is Fredholm of index zero. By [F6] and the compactness of $K_A$ from step 1.1, $\Delta_A=\Delta_{A_0}+K_A$ is Fredholm of index zero. [F3, F6, step 1.1]

blocks: [F3] The Coulomb splitting is $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)=\ker d_A^*\oplus\operatorname{im}d_A$, with bounded projection $d_AG_Ad_A^*$. [[lem-qftx-covariant-laplacian-sobolev-splitting]]
associated_steps: 1.2 The tangent space of the Coulomb slice at $A$ is $\ker d_A^*$. By [F3], the bounded linear map $L_A:\ker d_A^*\oplus H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)\to H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$, $L_A(a,\xi)=a+d_A\xi$, is an isomorphism with inverse $v\mapsto(v-d_AG_Ad_A^*v,G_Ad_A^*v)$. The derivative of $(a,\xi)\mapsto(A+a)^{\exp\xi}$ at $(0,0)$ is $L_A$ by [F1]. [F1, F3]

1.3 Define $F(a,\xi):=d_A^*((A+a)^{\exp\xi}-A)$ for $a\in H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ near $0$ and $\xi\in H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ near $0$. This is a smooth map into $H^{k-1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ by [F1], and $F(0,0)=0$. Its partial derivative in $\xi$ at $(0,0)$ is $d_A^*d_A=\Delta_A$, an isomorphism by [F3]. The implicit-function theorem [F4] therefore gives, for every connection sufficiently near $A$, a unique nearby gauge parameter moving it into the Coulomb condition $d_A^*(B^u-A)=0$. This supplies a local section of the orbit projection. [F1, F3, F4]

2.1 Apply the inverse-function theorem [F4] to $\Phi_A(s,u):=s^u$ on the local Banach product $S_{A,\varepsilon}\times\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ near $(A,e)$; its derivative is $L_A$ from step 1.2. Shrink $\varepsilon$ so the slice remains in the open irreducible locus. At $(s,e)$, for $s=A+a$, the derivative is $L_s(b,\xi)=b+d_s\xi$ on $b\in\ker d_A^*$; this differs from $L_A$ only by $(b,\xi)\mapsto[a,\xi]$. Its operator norm is at most $C\|a\|_{H^k}$ by [F7]. Choose $\varepsilon$ so $C\varepsilon\|L_A^{-1}\|<1$; then [F5] makes $L_s$ an isomorphism for every $s$ in the slice. At an arbitrary $(s,u_0)$, write $u=u_0v$ near $u_0$ and use $s^{u_0v}=(s^{u_0})^v$. Applying the inverse action by $u_0$ to the target tangent and changing the gauge tangent by the invertible adjoint action identifies this derivative with $L_s$. Hence the derivative is an isomorphism at every point of the slice product, and the inverse-function theorem makes $\Phi_A$ a local diffeomorphism throughout. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F7, step 1.2]

blocks: [F1] The Grassmannian graph charts and projective bundle of line quotients construct the universal proper flat projective-line family. [[lem-grassmannian-standard-affine-charts]], [[def-projective-bundle-scheme]], [[thm-projective-bundle-represents-line-quotients]], [[thm-projective-morphism-proper]]
associated_steps: 1.1 Algebraize the holomorphic bundle using [A1]. Its algebraic sheaf is locally free: the holomorphic bundle is dualizable, the exact tensor equivalence transports its evaluation and coevaluation and reflects their triangle identities, and those identities give a finite dual basis on each local algebraic chart, hence a finite projective module. In a splitting C⁴=A⊕B into two-planes, a graph chart of G consists of X:A→B and the incidence is (X,[λ])↦[λ,Xλ], with p a product with P(A). In the library quotient convention it is the projective bundle of the dual of the tautological subbundle. Thus [F1] gives properness, finite presentation and flatness, and e*E is a coherent locally free sheaf flat over G. [A1, F1, construct]

3.1 Evaluation p*H→e*E is a map of rank-N bundles and is invertible on L, since on its analytification it evaluates all constant sections of the trivial bundle. Its determinant-zero locus is closed. Properness of p makes the image closed in the parameter neighborhood; remove that image to obtain an entire neighboring family on which evaluation is an isomorphism. This is a local neighborhood of every real line, not a claim about all complex lines. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

blocks: [[lem-qftx-twistor-line-section-direct-image]]

[F3] Absolute GAGA, algebraic line-family cohomology/base change and the elementary local P¹ product argument give the actual analytic section bundle and evaluation isomorphism near every real line; surjectivity is proved, not assumed. The scalar O(-1) degree-zero and degree-one groups vanish. [[lem-qftx-twistor-line-section-direct-image]], [[thm-cohomology-projective-space-twisting-sheaves]]
associated_steps: 2.1 For any Ward bundle use [F3] to form the analytic vector bundle H over a complex-open neighborhood U of every real line in G=Gr(2,4), with holomorphic evaluation p*H≅e*E on the universal family. On a graph chart X:A→B, incidence is (X,[λ])↦[λ,Xλ]. The distribution D=ker(de) consists of matrix variations v with vλ=0 and no λ variation. It is a holomorphic involutive rank-two subbundle, since it is tangent to the fibers of the submersion e. The restriction of p*Ω¹_U to D has kernel B*⊗O(-1) on each projective-line fiber and target D*≅O(1)². The O(-1) vanishings in [F3] give Ω¹_U≅p_*D*. Equivalently, on the graph chart a linear covector on Hom(A,B) restricts to a section on all kernels vλ=0; the map is injective because those kernels span Hom(A,B), and both coefficient spaces have dimension four. This gives the holomorphic sheaf isomorphism without any extra analytic base-change assumption. [A1, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The bundle e*E has a canonical flat partial connection δ along D: in a holomorphic frame pulled back from E, differentiate coefficient functions along the fibers of e. Changes of that frame have zero D derivative, so δ is well-defined and flat. Transfer δ to p*H by evaluation. For a local holomorphic section s of H, δ(p*s) is a section of D*⊗p*H. Push down using Ω¹_U≅p_*D* from step 2.1 to define ∇s. The partial Leibniz rule becomes ∇(fs)=df⊗s+f∇s, so ∇ is a holomorphic full connection. Its pullback restriction to D is δ, first on pulled-back sections and then on all sections by Leibniz. It is unique: the difference of two such connections is an End(H)-valued one-form restricting to zero on D at every λ, hence zero by the same cotangent isomorphism. The curvature restricts on D to δ²=0. Connections on overlapping graph charts agree by uniqueness. [F3, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Restrict H and ∇ to the totally real graph locus M=HP¹. Its smooth real incidence is diffeomorphic to Z by (P,[v])↦[v], with inverse [v]↦(span(v,jv),[v]); the explicit charts in [F3] verify smoothness. Under this identification dp(D) is exactly the span of H₁,H₂ in step 1.1: write X_z=((z₁,-bar_z₂),(z₂,bar_z₁)) and solve v(1,w)^T=0. Therefore the restricted smooth connection has F(H₁,H₂)=0 for every w, so all three self-dual coefficients in step 1.1 vanish. Hence it is ASD. Evaluation intertwines the original holomorphic operator on E with the reconstructed vertical/horizontal Dolbeault operator: it is holomorphic vertically, and on D its derivative is exactly the canonical relative derivative δ by step 3.1. These directions generate the (0,1) tangent in step 1.1, proving equality of the full operators, not just of underlying bundles. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 To identify the connection with the first-neighborhood prescription, the line's conormal bundle is O(-1)², by its two independent linear defining equations. The sequence 0→E|L⊗(I/I²)→E|L^(1)→E|L→0 and [F3]'s O(-1) vanishings give a unique extension of every line section to L^(1). Smooth variation is supplied by step 3.1, not merely inferred from this pointwise uniqueness. At a graph X choose a local holomorphic section s of H with specified value and ∇s(X)=0; in a local frame its affine-linear coefficient function can realize any prescribed first jet. Its evaluation derivative in parameter direction v vanishes on vλ=0 by step 3.1, so factors through the normal displacement vλ. These factorizations glue on the two λ charts and give precisely a first-neighborhood extension. Uniqueness identifies it with the preceding extension. Subtracting such a horizontal first jet from an arbitrary section shows that differentiation relative to this extension is exactly ∇. This proves the prescription, its Leibniz rule, chart independence and smooth dependence. [F3, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

5.2 The section metric is the form induced by b_z(s(z),t(σz)) in [F1]. It is independent of z on each line because that scalar is holomorphic on P¹, and is smooth by the evaluation frames of [F3]. The preceding construction commutes with duals, conjugate pullback and bundle morphisms: each commutes with the canonical relative e-connection and the cotangent isomorphism, and uniqueness in step 3.1 then forces the full connections to commute. Apply this to the holomorphic reality isomorphism E→σ*bar_E*. On the real line locus, the induced conjugate involution fixes the parameter and its real tangent vectors. Thus the induced map H→bar_H* intertwines ∇ with the conjugate dual connection, which is precisely X h(s,t)=h(∇_X s,t)+h(s,∇_X t) for real X. Positivity from [F1] makes ∇ unitary. Arbitrary independent positive forms would not satisfy this identity and are not used. [F1, F3, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Starting from A in step 1.1, its constant real-line sections identify the reconstructed smooth H with E. Along every alpha-plane the recovered connection has the same derivative as A; the cotangent uniqueness in step 3.1 makes the full connections equal. The unitary reality pairing and framing also agree. These constructions and identities apply to morphisms as well, so descend to inverse maps on based unitary gauge and framed holomorphic isomorphism classes. No irreducibility or absence of parallel sections was used. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.2, algebra]

associated_steps: 1.2 Let $L\cong\mathbb P^1$ be any real twistor line. Its normal bundle in $\mathbb P^3$ is $\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$, and the conormal sequence splits because its extension group is $H^1(\mathcal O(1))^{\oplus2}=0$. Hence $\Omega_Z^1|_L\cong\mathcal O(-2)\oplus\mathcal O(-1)^{\oplus2}$ and $T_Z|_L\cong\mathcal O(2)\oplus\mathcal O(1)^{\oplus2}$. Since $\Omega_Z^2\cong T_Z(-4)$, each of $\mathcal E(-1)|_L$, $\mathcal E(-3)|_L$, $\mathcal E(-2)|_L$, $(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1))|_L$, and $(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2)|_L$ is a sum of negative line bundles. The Serre-dual bundles restrict respectively to $\mathcal E^*(-3)$, $\mathcal E^*(-1)$, $\mathcal E^*(-2)$, $\mathcal E^*\otimes T_Z(-3)$, and $\mathcal E^*\otimes\Omega_Z^1$, also sums of negative line bundles. Every point of $Z$ lies on a real line, so negativity on every such line makes every global section zero. Thus [F6] gives $H^0(Z,F)=0$ and [F5] gives $H^3(Z,F)=0$ for all the listed coefficient bundles $F$. [A2, F5, F6, algebra]

2.1 Choose a plane $P\cong\mathbb P^2$ containing a real twistor line. By [A2] and the direct-image result, an open family of lines near that line has evaluation isomorphisms and hence trivial restrictions of $\mathcal E$. Those lines form a nonempty complex-open subset of the line family of $P$. Choose affine coordinates $(x,y)$ with the original line given by $y=0$. This open family contains the projective lines $y=b$ for all sufficiently small complex $b$, so their union contains a nonempty open subset of $P$. A section of $\mathcal E(-2)|_P$ vanishes on each such line because $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(-2)^{\oplus N})=0$. It therefore vanishes on that open subset. In a connected coordinate chart and holomorphic bundle frame, [F8] makes its zero-germ locus closed as well as open. The plane is connected (any two points lie on a connected projective line), so the section vanishes everywhere; no density assertion for an arbitrary complex-open line family is needed. The divisor sequence $0\to\mathcal E(-3)\to\mathcal E(-2)\to\mathcal E(-2)|_P\to0$ and step 1.1 now give $H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-3))=0$. [A2, F6, F8, step 1.1, algebra]

blocks: [F5] [[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]: on an open Minkowski coordinate region, compactly supported $C^1$ coefficients admit differentiation under the integral sign and integration by parts; if a continuous scalar coefficient integrates to zero against every smooth compactly supported scalar test, it vanishes pointwise.
associated_steps:
2.1 The difference of the two action densities vanishes outside the compact support of $a$ and its derivatives. Apply the parameter-differentiation clause of [F5] to its smooth coordinate coefficients. Symmetry of $\kappa$ and the even degree of $F_i$ then give
$\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_0\Delta(S/\hbar)_i(\varepsilon;a)
=-\frac{1}{g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int
\kappa(D_{A_i}a\wedge *_\eta F_i)$. [A1, A3, A4, F1, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Write the compactly supported scalar three-form as
$\kappa(a\wedge *_\eta F_i)=\sum_{\mu=0}^3h_\mu\widehat{dx^\mu}$ with
$h_\mu\in C_c^1(U_i)$. Its exterior derivative is
$\sum_\mu(\partial_\mu h_\mu)d^4x$. Apply the integration-by-parts clause
of [F5] with the constant function $1$ to each coefficient $h_\mu$; each
integral is zero, so $\int d\kappa(a\wedge *_\eta F_i)=0$. Substitution in
step 2.1 yields
$\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_0\Delta(S/\hbar)_i(\varepsilon;a)
=-\frac{1}{g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int
\kappa(a\wedge D_{A_i} *_\eta F_i)$. [A1, A4, F5, step 2.1, step 1.2]

4.2 Conversely, assume stationarity. In a local coordinate chart and the orthonormal basis from [F1], write
$J_i=D_{A_i} *_\eta F_i
=\sum_{\mu=0}^3\sum_{b=1}^3J_{\mu b}T_b\,\widehat{dx^\mu}$,
where $\widehat{dx^\mu}$ is the oriented coordinate three-form satisfying
$dx^\mu\wedge\widehat{dx^\mu}=d^4x$. For fixed $\mu,b$, choose
$a=\psi T_b dx^\mu$ with arbitrary smooth compactly supported real $\psi$.
Stationarity and step 3.1 give $\int\psi J_{\mu b}\,d^4x=0$ for every such
$\psi$. The fundamental-lemma clause of [F5] implies $J_{\mu b}=0$
throughout the chart. All coefficients vanish, so the local equation holds.
[A4, F1, F5, step 3.1, algebra]

vacuum of this potential must set all three derivatives and

associated_steps: 1.1 The inverse change of variables is $M=(q+p)/\sqrt2$ and $e^{i\beta}\overline{\widetilde M}=(q-p)/\sqrt2$. It preserves the sum of charged kinetic norms and gives $|M|^2+|\widetilde M|^2=s$. Set $z=e^{-i\beta}M\widetilde M$. The charged part of the potential in [F1] at linear $u$ is $2g^2|z-v^2|^2+g^2(|M|^2-|\widetilde M|^2)^2/2=g^2s^2/2+2g^2v^4-4g^2v^2\operatorname{Re}z$. Since $2\operatorname{Re}z=|q|^2-|p|^2$ and $\xi=2v^2$, this is $g^2(s-\xi)^2/2+2g^2\xi|p|^2$. The remaining scalar potential is $2|a|^2s$ and its gradient term is $g^{-2}|\partial_i a|^2$. 2.1 For either charged field $f=q,p$, expand $|(D_1+iD_2)f|^2=|Df|^2-B|f|^2+i\{\partial_1(\bar fD_2f)-\partial_2(\bar fD_1f)\}$. Expanding $[B-g^2(\xi-s)]^2/(2g^2)$ gives $B^2/(2g^2)+g^2(\xi-s)^2/2+Bs-\xi B$. Step 1.1 shows all the required nonnegative densities are integrable. If $G(R)=\int_{|x|=R}(|Dq|^2+|Dp|^2)ds$, then [F9] and finite energy give $\int G(R)dR<\infty$. Hence there are increasing radii $R_j\to\infty$ with $R_jG(R_j)\to0$, since an eventual positive lower bound on $RG(R)$ would force logarithmic divergence. Uniform vacuum amplitudes and [F8] bound the boundary-current integral by $C\sqrt{R_jG(R_j)}\to0$. Integrating the two algebraic identities on those disks, using [F11], limiting flux $2\pi n$ and [F10] gives the stated whole-plane identity. For negative n, conjugation reverses flux and changes $D_1+iD_2$ to $D_1-iD_2$ without changing energy. [A1, F1, F2, F8, F9, F10, F11, step 1.1, algebra]

5.1 In the nonlinear potential [F1], put $H=\sqrt2M\widetilde M+\mu u'(a)$. Differentiation gives $\partial_{\bar a}(g^2H\bar H)=g^2H\bar\mu\,\overline{u''(a)}$. The derivative of $2|a|^2s$ is $2as$, which vanishes at $a=0$; all gradient terms also have zero first variation at identically zero $a$. Thus the displayed derivative is the remaining Euler–Lagrange source. If it is nonzero somewhere, a smooth compactly supported variation of the complex field $a$ supported in a small neighborhood makes the first variation nonzero, proving nonstationarity. For the screening distinction, the constant vacuum has $q=\sqrt\xi$, $p=a=0$. With $A_c=A/g$, its charged gradient term contributes $-g^2\xi A_{c,\mu}A_c^\mu$, hence $m_D^2=2g^2\xi$ by the Proca normalization. The linearized unit static source equation is $(-\Delta+m_D^2)A_{c,0}=\delta_0$ in three spatial dimensions. Radial differentiation verifies $G(r)=e^{-m_Dr}/(4\pi r)$ solves the homogeneous equation for $r>0$; $-4\pi r^2G^{\prime}(r)\to1$ and the locally integrable mass term establish the unit delta distribution at the origin. Its exponential decay proves screening only in this linear response. The cylinder statement instead fixes dual magnetic/original electric flux; it supplies no quantum observable or control of omitted nonlinear and higher-derivative terms. [given, F1, F2, algebra] ∎

blocks: [F6] [[lem-qsmx-finite-group-irrep-dimension-square-sum]]: for a finite group $H$, there are finitely many irreducible complex representations and the sum of the squares of their dimensions is $|H|$.
associated_steps: 3.2 By [F5], every finite-dimensional complex representation of $S_3$ is semisimple. The three pairwise nonisomorphic irreducibles in step 2.1 have squared dimensions $1,1,4$, whose sum is $6=|S_3|$; [F6] therefore leaves no other irreducible isomorphism class. Kernels and cokernels of equivariant maps inherit the $S_3$ action, so this representation category is abelian. Each Hom space is a finite-dimensional subspace of a linear-map space, and tensor product is bilinear. The trivial representation is a simple unit. For any representation $W$, give its dual $W^*$ the action $(g\cdot\ell)(w)=\ell(g^{-1}\cdot w)$. Evaluation $W^*\otimes W\to\mathbb C$, $\ell\otimes w\mapsto\ell(w)$, is equivariant because $(g\cdot\ell)(g\cdot w)=\ell(w)$. For a basis $e_i$ of $W$ and dual basis $e^i$, coevaluation $1\mapsto\sum_i e_i\otimes e^i$ is invariant: under $g$ this tensor corresponds to the conjugate $\rho(g)I_W\rho(g)^{-1}=I_W$. The two snake composites are identities by $\sum_i e^i(w)e_i=w$ and $\sum_i\ell(e_i)e^i=\ell$. Thus every representation has left and right duals and the category meets [F1]. [given, F1, F5, F6, step 2.1, algebra]

blocks: [F2] [[thm-complete-reducibility-and-reynolds-operator-for-complex-reductive-group]]: assuming AC and complex reductive affine algebraic $G$, every rational $G$-module has a natural Reynolds projection onto its invariant subspace, and a surjective equivariant map of rational $G$-modules induces a surjective map of invariant subspaces.

blocks: [F4] Normal complex matrices have orthonormal eigenbases; Hermitian eigenvalues are real, by taking the inner product of an eigenvector with its image. Finite matrix exponential series converge with their differential identities. [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]], [[lem-xd-finite-matrix-exponential-series]]
associated_steps: 2.1 Define $F_\zeta(g)=M(g)^2-\zeta\log\det(g^\dagger g)$. It is continuous and invariant under left $U(V)$. By [F4], the positive eigenvalues of $g^\dagger g$ are at most $\|g\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2$, so $\det(g^\dagger g)\le\|g\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{2k}$. The column bound in step 1.1 therefore gives $\log\det(g^\dagger g)\le C_x+2k^2\log(1+M(g))$, with $C_x=2k\log\max\{1,A_x\}$. Since $\log(1+M)\le M$ for $M\ge0$, a sublevel $F_\zeta\le c$ with $\zeta>0$ bounds $M$ by the quadratic inequality $M^2-2\zeta k^2M-\zeta C_x\le c$, and hence bounds $g$. The same sublevel gives $\det(g^\dagger g)\ge e^{-c/\zeta}>0$; bounded entries and the adjugate formula therefore bound $g^{-1}$. The sublevel is closed in the finite matrix space, since any matrix limit remains invertible by this determinant bound. It is compact by [F3]. The nonempty sublevel at $F_\zeta(I)$ has a minimum, which is a global minimum since all points outside have larger value. For $\zeta=0$ and regular $x$, $F_0=M^2$ directly bounds $M$, and the two word bounds in step 1.1 bound both $g$ and $g^{-1}$; the same closedness/compactness argument gives a minimum. [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Let $H=H^\dagger$ and vary $g$ by $e^{tH}g$. Differentiating the finite trace expressions gives $\frac{d}{dt}F_\zeta(e^{tH}g)|_{t=0}=2\operatorname{tr}(H(\mu_{\mathbb R}(x')-\zeta I))$: a $B_i'$ term contributes $2\operatorname{tr}H[B_i',B_i'^\dagger]$, the $I'$ term contributes $2\operatorname{tr}HI'I'^\dagger$, the $J'$ term contributes $-2\operatorname{tr}HJ'^\dagger J'$, and $\log\det(g^\dagger e^{2tH}g)$ has derivative $2\operatorname{tr}H$. Thus each minimum from step 2.1 is balanced, because the trace pairing on Hermitian matrices is nondegenerate. Conversely a balanced point is critical: these Hermitian directions and the skew-Hermitian directions tangent to the left unitary orbit span every real tangent direction of $GL(V)$, and the latter derivatives vanish by unitary invariance. The matrix exponentials in these calculations are justified by [F4]; complex matrices may equivalently be represented by their real block matrices. [F1, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Diagonalize $H$ by [F4], with real eigenvalues $\lambda_i$. Along the preceding path the squared $B_i'$ entries have factors $e^{2t(\lambda_a-\lambda_b)}$, the squared $I'$ entries have $e^{2t\lambda_a}$ and the squared $J'$ entries have $e^{-2t\lambda_a}$. The log determinant is affine in $t$. Hence $F_\zeta''$ is a sum of $4w^2|z|^2e^{2tw}$ over those entries and their listed weights $w$, and is nonnegative. It can vanish only when $[H,B_i']=0$, $HI'=0$ and $J'H=0$. Stability of $x'$ then forces $H=0$, by applying $H$ to all spanning word vectors. Thus the path is strictly convex for every nonzero $H$. Given two critical matrices $g_1,g_2$, diagonalize the positive matrix $(g_2g_1^{-1})^\dagger(g_2g_1^{-1})$ and take the positive logarithms of its eigenvalues to write $g_2g_1^{-1}=u e^H$ with $u$ unitary and $H$ Hermitian. The endpoints of $e^{tH}g_1$ are both critical, after removing $u$ by invariance. Strict convexity forces $H=0$, so $g_2=ug_1$. This proves uniqueness of the unitary orbit at either level. [F2, F4, step 3.1, algebra]

6.1 At a balanced datum $x$, let $L_x:\operatorname{Herm}(V)\to\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ be $H\mapsto\frac{d}{dt}\mu_{\mathbb R}(e^{tH}\cdot x)|_{t=0}$. Step 4.1 gives $2\operatorname{tr}(H L_xH)=F_\zeta''(e^{tH})|_{t=0}>0$ for nonzero $H$, so $L_x$ is injective and hence invertible in finite equal dimensions. The map $(H,y)\mapsto\mu_{\mathbb R}(e^H\cdot y)-\zeta I$ is smooth. To see smoothness of the exponential in the matrix entries directly, differentiate its absolutely convergent power series: on a bounded matrix set, an order-$r$ derivative of its degree-$m$ term is bounded by a constant times $m^r R^{m-r}/m!$, a summable majorant; this applies through real block matrices as in [F4]. By [F5] the balancing $H=H(y)$ is locally $C^r$ for every finite $r$, and uniqueness glues these branches to the same smooth map. The same invertible derivative along the Hermitian gauge directions in $T_xX^s$ proves that the real-level locus is a smooth submanifold. The unitary group is compact (closed bounded matrices), its action there is free by [F2] and proper (inverse images are closed subsets of $U(V)$ times a compact coordinate projection); therefore its quotient is smooth by [F6]. The map to the complex quotient is smooth using local submersion sections in [F6]. On any word-frame chart [F2], the local balancing map just constructed, followed by the unitary quotient map, is its smooth inverse; step 4.1 proves independence of all choices. Thus the bijections are diffeomorphisms. The compact torus commutes with gauge actions and preserves both the complex equation and $\mu_{\mathbb R}$, so the bijections are equivariant. For $k=0$ all matrices and equations are empty and all quotients are points, proving every boundary case stated. No sheaf or ASD identification was used. associated_steps: 6.1 Each $S_C$ is the affine scheme cut out in the original matrix space by $\mu=0$ and $C=I$. blocks: [F1] For $r\geq1$, $BT=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r$ has a countable CW structure whose CW topology is the ordinary product topology; the complete product-topology argument is given in the supplier's proof. [[lem-universal-complex-flag-bundle-is-bt-n]]
associated_steps: 1.1 If $r=0$, $BT$ is a point and the CW and paracompact assertions reduce to the compact manifold $F$. For $r\geq1$, [F1] gives $BT$ its ordinary product CW topology, and [F3] makes it paracompact Hausdorff. By [F2], choose a finite CW complex $K$ and a homotopy equivalence $h:F\to K$. Since $K$ is finite, its CW product with the CW complex $BT$ has the ordinary product topology; hence $BT\times K$ is a CW complex. The maps $\mathrm{id}_{BT}\times h$ and the product of a homotopy inverse with $\mathrm{id}_{BT}$ are homotopy inverses, since their coordinate homotopies are continuous in the product topology. Thus $BT\times F$ has CW type. If $F=\varnothing$, take $K=\varnothing$. [A1, F1, F2, F3, construct]

2.1 If $F=\varnothing$, the product is empty and paracompact Hausdorff, so assume $F\ne\varnothing$. To prove paracompactness of $BT\times F$, let $\mathcal U$ be an open cover. For each $x\in BT$ and $y\in F$, choose a product neighborhood $O_{x,y}\times V_{x,y}$ of $(x,y)$ contained in some member $U_{x,y}\in\mathcal U$. Compactness of $F$ selects finitely many $y_1,\ldots,y_m$ whose $V_{x,y_j}$ cover $F$. Then $O_x=\bigcap_{j=1}^m O_{x,y_j}$ is an open neighborhood of $x$, and $O_x\times F$ is covered by $U_{x,y_1},\ldots,U_{x,y_m}$. Paracompactness of $BT$ gives a locally finite open refinement $\{W_\alpha\}$ of $\{O_x\}$. For each $\alpha$, choose $x_\alpha$ with $W_\alpha\subseteq O_{x_\alpha}$; the finitely many sets $(W_\alpha\times F)\cap U_{x_\alpha,y_j}$ cover $W_\alpha\times F$, are open, and refine $\mathcal U$. They are locally finite because a neighborhood $N\times F$ meets sets indexed by only those $\alpha$ for which $W_\alpha$ meets $N$, a finite set. Hence $BT\times F$ is paracompact. It is Hausdorff as a product of Hausdorff spaces. The point and rank-zero cases satisfy the same conclusions. [F1, F3, given, construct] ∎

blocks: [F4] The product Milnor bundle $ET\to BT$ is numerable, and $BT=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r$ has its ordinary countable CW topology. For closed $H\subseteq T$, $T/H$ is a compact smooth manifold; the local finite-nerve lemma gives it CW type. The quotient $ET/H\cong ET\times_T(T/H)\to BT$ is a numerable locally trivial bundle with compact fiber $T/H$. The compact-fiber bundle theorem therefore makes $ET/H$ paracompact Hausdorff, CGWH, and of CW type. Also $ET\to ET/H$ is a locally trivial principal $H$-bundle. associated_steps: 2.1 Consider any invariant open set $W\subseteq V_j\cong T\times_{H_j}D(V_j^0)$. Its inverse image in the slice has the form $T\times_{H_j}W_0$ for an $H_j$-invariant open $W_0\subseteq D(V_j^0)$. The Borel identification is the homeomorphism $[e,[t,w]]\mapsto[e\cdot t,w]$ from $ET\times_T(T\times_{H_j}W_0)$ to $ET\times_{H_j}W_0$, with inverse $[e,w]\mapsto[e,[1,w]]$; the quotient relations show both maps are well-defined. Write $B_H=ET/H$. The map $B_H\to BT$ is the associated quotient bundle $ET\times_T(T/H)\to BT$, and [F4] gives its compact-fiber CW-type and paracompactness properties. Since $ET\to BT$ is numerable, this associated quotient bundle is numerable as well: its local product charts over each Milnor chart retain the same subordinate partition. By [F4], $ET\to B_H$ is locally a principal $H$-bundle: over a Milnor $T$-chart it has form $U\times T\to U\times(T/H)$, and local sections of the Lie quotient $T\to T/H$ give the principal $H$-charts. The projection $q:B_H\to BT$ pulls $L_\chi$ back to the associated line $ET\times_H\mathbb C_{\chi|_H}$; the explicit trivialization $[e,z]\mapsto([e]_H,z)$ is well-defined because $\chi|_H=1$. Thus this is a numerable trivial line bundle, using its global chart and the constant partition $1$. The space $B_H$ is path-connected as a continuous image of contractible $ET$, so [F5] applies and its first Chern class is zero. Under the Borel identification, the projection $ET\times_H W_0\to BT$ factors through $B_H$, and the character class on $ET\times_H W_0$ is the pullback of this zero class. It therefore acts as zero on $H_T^*(W;k)$. As $\chi$ is nontrivial, this class becomes invertible in $\mathscr S_T(k)$, and the localized module is zero. [F2, F3, F4, F5, given, construct]
